title: Model Promotion: Canary, Chaos and Load Validation Protocol
author: Aisha Kumar
summary: This document defines the canonical protocol for promoting a candidate model from staging to production in Redwood inference environments. The protocol combines canary traffic validation, targeted chaos experiments, and load-scaling verification to ensure models meet functional, performance, cost, and robustness requirements before full promotion.
intent: Provide a repeatable, auditable process that reduces risk when rolling out new model versions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Ensure compatibility with quantized artifacts, KV-cache behavior, and downstream prompt sets and metrics used by product features.
scope: Applies to all model promotions handled by the Model Onboarding and Serving teams: text generation and chat models, embedding variants, and quantized model builds. Does NOT replace safety evaluations or legal/compliance checks (those must be completed separately).
definitions: Candidate model: the specific model artifact/weight bundle being promoted. Canary cohort: a small percentage of production traffic routed to the candidate. Chaos test: deliberate fault injection into dependencies or resources (network latency, GPU eviction simulation). Metrics baseline: historical SLI windows against which the candidate is compared.
prerequisites:
- Production baseline dataset and key prompt sets prepared (see 'related_pages')
- Candidate model registered in model-catalog with version tag and quantization profile attached
- Monitoring hooks instrumented: latency, p95/p99, error-rate, token-cost, quality scores (BLEU/ROUGE/CLARITY where applicable)
- Rollout policy defined in Redwood Console (traffic split, automatic fallback thresholds)
- Stakeholder approval (owners and reviewers listed in this doc)
protocol_overview: High-level phases: 1) Staging validation and synthetic stress, 2) Canary traffic validation (functional & quality), 3) Chaos experiments (dependence and degradation), 4) Load scaling validation (autoscale/steady-state), 5) Full promotion or rollback. Each phase has pass/fail criteria and required artifacts recorded in the promotion ticket.
validation_steps:
1) Staging smoke: run the eval-harness smoke suite against the candidate (sanity prompts, adversarial prompt subset, and quantization integrity tests). Record the run id.

2) Canary setup: define a canary cohort (default 1% traffic) and snapshot baseline SLI window (previous 7 days). Configure canary to route to both original and candidate for identical request sampling where possible.

3) Functional quality check (0–24h): evaluate prompt-set agreement and business metrics: acceptance threshold default: quality score drift <= 2% absolute and false-positive/undesired-behavior rate delta <= 0.5 percentage points. If the candidate fails, abort and open regression triage.

4) Latency & cost check (0–24h): ensure p95 latency regression <= +15ms or +10% (whichever is smaller), p99 within SLA bounds. Token-cost-per-response must not exceed configured budget for the route (see config_table).

5) Chaos tests (24–48h): run two targeted chaos experiments: a) network elevation: inject 50–150ms additional latency to model host egress paths; b) scheduler preemption simulation: reduce available GPU capacity by 25% for a 30-minute window. Expected outcome: graceful degradation on candidate equal or better than baseline; automatic fallback must trigger per routing policy without elevated error budget.

6) Load validation (48–72h): increase traffic to 25% of production via staged ramp (1% -> 5% -> 15% -> 25%), each stage held for >= 30 minutes of stable metrics. Verify autoscaling behavior and observe queue/backpressure metrics.

7) Final decision gate: if all checks pass and no new class of failure is observed, promote to 100% with a 30-minute guarded window for automated rollback if SLOs degrade beyond thresholds.
failures_and_mitigation:
Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Quality regressions on specific prompt sets: run prompt-slicing to isolate failing prompts, revert candidate or pin model to a narrower quant profile; file a regression-triage ticket referencing the eval-harness run id.
- Tokenization/response truncation with long context: verify KV-cache compatibility and sequence-length handling; if failure present, fall back to non-quantized variant or adjust sequence-limits in route config.
- Latency spike under load: reduce canary traffic and enable slower-safe-fallback routing policy (route to smaller-latency variant); open performance bug with runtime team.
- Chaos-induced cascading failures: immediately enable global fallback to baseline model and execute incident playbook 'eng-oncall/incident-process'.
metrics_and_slos:
Key metrics captured during each phase (thresholds are defaults; product owners may tighten):
- Functional quality: variant-accuracy (or task-specific metric) — drift <= 2% absolute
- Safety regressions: new safety-flagged responses <= 0.1% of sampled requests
- Latency: p95 <= baseline + 15ms or +10% (min of the two), p99 within SLA (route-specific)
- Error-rate: 5xx rate increase <= +0.05 percentage points
- Cost: tokens-per-response change <= +8%
- Availability: success-rate >= 99.95% during ramp windows

All metrics must be annotated with eval-harness run ids and monitoring-snapshot ids for auditability.
config_table:
| Field | Purpose | Default/Recommended | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| canary_percent | Fraction of production traffic to route during canary | 1% -> 25% staged | Start at 1% and only increase when all checks pass |
| canary_hold_min | Minimum hold time per stage | 30m | Use longer holds if traffic patterns are bursty |
| quality_drift_threshold | Absolute allowed drift on quality metric | 2% | Configurable per-product |
| latency_regression_limit | Allowed p95 regression | min(+15ms, +10%) | Combined absolute and relative limits |
| chaos_latency_inject | Simulated added latency during chaos | 50-150ms | Run two levels (moderate/strong) depending on risk appetite |
| autoscale_headroom | Extra capacity to reserve during load test | +20% above normal | Prevents false negatives due to transient limits |
example_configs:
YAML example for a canary rollout in Redwood Console:

---
route: chat-completion-v1
baseline_model: redwood/chat-7b-v1
candidate_model: redwood/chat-7b-v2-quant8
canary:
  stages:
    - percent: 1
      hold: 30m
    - percent: 5
      hold: 30m
    - percent: 15
      hold: 45m
    - percent: 25
      hold: 60m
rollback_policy:
  on_quality_drift: immediate
  on_latency_spike: staged_revert
  fallback_model: redwood/chat-7b-v1
metrics_to_monitor: [latency_p95, latency_p99, success_rate, quality_score, token_cost]
---
cli_commands_and_tooling_examples:
- Run eval-harness smoke suite: 
  ./bin/eval-harness run --suite staging-smoke --model redwood/chat-7b-v2-quant8 --out runs/2026-01-18-smoke.json

- Snapshot monitoring baseline: 
  redwoodctl metrics snapshot --route chat-completion-v1 --window 7d --out snapshots/baseline-2026-01-18.json

- Create canary in console (example using redwoodctl):
  redwoodctl rollout create --route chat-completion-v1 --candidate redwood/chat-7b-v2-quant8 --canary-percent 1 --hold 30m --annotations "eval_run=runs/2026-01-18-smoke.json"

- Run network latency chaos (internal tooling):
  chaosctl inject --target model-host:10.0.5.12 --type latency --ms 100 --duration 30m --annotation "promo=test-2026-01-18"
troubleshooting_and_triage: If a regression is observed: 1) Collect eval-harness artifacts, monitoring snapshots, and sampled responses. 2) Execute prompt-slicing on failing prompts to localize failure modes. 3) If quantization suspected, rebuild with alternate quant profile (e.g., from 'per-workload-quant-tuner') and re-run smoke tests. 4) If the issue is unclear, escalate to regression-triage channel and assign to runtime or research teams depending on artifact. Include run ids and model-catalog commit id in the ticket.
rollback_and_postpromo_actions:
- Automatic rollback triggers: any quality drift beyond threshold or sustained p99 latency beyond route SLA for 10 minutes.
- Post-promotion: schedule 72-hour watch with daily summaries; run full eval-harness suite (including adversarial and long-context stress tests) within 24 hours of full promotion.
- Documentation: attach all run ids, snapshots, and canary decision notes to the promotion ticket. Update model-catalog metadata with final promotion timestamp.
